title: Product listings expose both a sample price and zero-price items
observation: The captured Glucare Plus product page text presents a 1-package listing at 9,000 VND and other product listings at 0 VND in the same product section.

impact.user: A self-purchaser or adult child cannot tell from the captured state whether zero is a real price, unavailable price, or placeholder.
impact.business: Ambiguous price presentation can interrupt purchase confidence.

suggested_direction: Replace zero-price merchandising states with an explicit availability or contact-for-price label and keep package/price meaning consistent.
unknowns: The capture does not establish inventory, configuration, or backend pricing state.
persona_impact: Both an older self-purchaser and an adult child buying for a parent need an unambiguous package and payable price before proceeding.
limitations: Cart mutation and checkout were not performed; no payable total was observed.
review_reasons: Observed issue is supported; preserve this candidate for the subsequent deduplication step under price-clarity.

persona_impacts.impact: Both an older self-purchaser and an adult child buying for a parent need an unambiguous package and payable price before proceeding.
An adult child comparing options for a parent needs consistent product/package/price information.

specialist_interpretations.interpretation: This ambiguity affects both an older self-purchaser and an adult child comparing products for a parent because the displayed amount conflicts with the surrounding paid offer context. The finding reports only the public display and makes no claim about backend price state.

review.reason: Observed issue is supported; preserve this candidate for the subsequent deduplication step under price-clarity.

impact.business: Unverifiable claim presentation can reduce trust for a health-related purchase.

limitations: Conclusion is limited to links and text in the captured browser state.

title: Mobile icon links lack accessible names
observation: The mobile accessibility artifact reports serious link-name failures for the cart, home, search, mobile-cart, and account icon links because the focusable elements have no discernible accessible text or ARIA label.

impact.user: Icon-only controls are harder to identify with assistive technology and provide weak explicit labeling for users with limited confidence.
impact.business: Unclear navigation and cart controls can obstruct product and purchase tasks.

suggested_direction: Give each icon control a localized accessible name and retain a clear visible or programmatic label across mobile states.
unknowns: The audit did not conduct a human screen-reader session.
persona_impact: A mobile user should not have to infer search, cart, account, or home actions from icon shape alone.
limitations: Impact is based on deterministic axe output and captured DOM, not a human assistive-technology test.
review_reasons: Observed issue is supported; preserve this candidate for the subsequent deduplication step under mobile-accessible-names.

persona_impacts.impact: A mobile user should not have to infer search, cart, account, or home actions from icon shape alone.

specialist_interpretations.interpretation: The header and fixed bottom bar make these utilities easy to find visually, which is positive. title: Product-price text fails automated contrast checks on mobile
observation: The mobile accessibility artifact reports serious color-contrast failures for product-price text, including gold text at 2.77:1 on the light background and gray text at 2.45:1, below the stated 3:1 or 4.5:1 thresholds.

impact.user: Low-contrast price text can be difficult to read, especially for visitors with reduced contrast sensitivity.
impact.business: Price legibility affects product comparison and confidence.
impact.technical: Rendered foreground/background combinations fail automated contrast rules.

suggested_direction: Adjust price colors or backgrounds so rendered text meets the applicable WCAG contrast ratio in every product-card state.
unknowns: Automated contrast results should be confirmed against final design tokens and states.
persona_impact: Middle-aged and older visitors need price information that remains legible without zoom or unusually high visual effort.
limitations: The result applies to the captured mobile rendering and does not measure individual visual ability.

title: The homepage hero does not show a principal product
observation: The stabilized desktop and mobile first-view captures show the ADDP logo, the message "Chăm sóc từ giá trị thiện lành", the headline "Sức Khỏe Bền Vững Khởi Nguồn Từ Tâm", an older couple, supporting copy, and the actions "Khám phá ngay" and "Tư vấn miễn phí". No product package or named principal product is visible in either captured first viewport. REQ-004 calls for the first viewport to combine a core message, a principal-product image, and a large clear CTA; the message and actions are present, while the product-image element is absent from the captured state.

impact.user: A first-time visitor can understand the care-oriented brand message, but must continue down the page before seeing what ADDP sells. This adds orientation work for an older or middle-aged self-purchaser and for an adult child quickly assessing a product for a parent.
impact.business: The first viewport does not immediately connect the brand promise to a specific purchasable product, weakening product discovery at the earliest decision point.

suggested_direction: Keep the current human, reassuring message, but add a clearly identifiable principal-product packshot or product grouping within the first desktop and mobile viewport and preserve an obvious route to that product.
unknowns: Whether another timed or carousel state shows a product before user interaction.
Whether the hero is intended to prioritize corporate positioning over immediate product orientation.
specialist_interpretation: The existing headline, supportive imagery, and two visible actions are positive orientation signals. Within the ADDP customer context, product identification is still a necessary part of first-view confidence because the researcher or purchaser may differ from the eventual product user.
limitations: This visual conclusion is limited to the saved stabilized viewport state at 1440x1000 and 390x1000; animation was frozen after stabilization, and the homepage had a material initial-to-stabilized difference.
The render remained partial with residual resource/decode failures, so this finding does not claim that every possible hero state lacks product imagery.
The first-time and high-intent journey interaction failures were excluded because they may be audit-induced and do not establish a site defect.
review_reasons: Observed issue is supported; preserve this candidate for the subsequent deduplication step under homepage-hero-products.

title: Mobile typography falls below the checklist's reading-size targets
observation: The Glucare mobile DOM records its hero heading at 23.4px and several ingredient headings at 15.5px. Those measured examples are below the checklist targets of 28–32px for mobile headings and 16px for body text. The examples support a product-page typography concern; no exhaustive text inventory is claimed.

impact.user: Small supporting copy and undersized headings increase reading effort on a phone, particularly for visitors with ordinary age-related vision changes or limited tolerance for dense health-product information.
impact.business: Visitors may scan past trust details, ingredient labels, or product distinctions that support confidence and purchase decisions.

suggested_direction: Raise mobile body and supporting text to at least 16px, bring primary and section headings into the 28-32px range where practical, and use 1.5-1.6 line height for reading copy while preserving the current responsive width behavior.
unknowns: The DOM text sampler does not inventory every visible text node, so the finding identifies evidenced examples rather than an exhaustive count.
User browser zoom, operating-system text scaling, and device pixel density were not varied.
specialist_interpretation: The three inspected mobile layouts fit their recorded viewport widths without horizontal overflow, which is positive. The remaining legibility burden comes from text sizing and line spacing rather than a broken responsive width in these captures.
limitations: Measurements come from the saved 390-400px mobile DOM captures only.
All relevant page collections remained partial; Glucare had pending images, and all three pages recorded residual resource/decode failures.
No claim is made about individual medical suitability or comprehension of the health statements.

title: Homepage hero actions are less prominent and less thumb-friendly than product-page CTAs
observation: In the stabilized mobile homepage DOM, "Khám phá ngay" measures about 142.5x38.2px and "Tư vấn miễn phí" about 134.6x32px; both use 13.5px text and appear as lightweight text/icon actions in the stabilized screenshot. By comparison, the saved mobile product pages show a 358x54.3px Glucare purchase action and a 303.6x54.4px Dovital purchase action as prominent filled controls. The homepage consultation action therefore does not match REQ-005's request for a large, rounded, strongly contrasting mobile action that is easy to press with a thumb, although the product-page purchase actions provide a positive implementation pattern.

impact.user: The two homepage choices are visible, but their smaller height and lighter button affordance demand more precision and provide less obvious prioritization for a phone user with ordinary or limited digital confidence.
impact.business: The homepage gives less visual emphasis to exploration and consultation than the product pages give to purchase, which may reduce progression from the first brand encounter.

suggested_direction: Apply the product pages' successful mobile CTA pattern to the homepage hero: use a clearly filled, rounded primary action with at least a 44px hit height, retain a distinct secondary consultation action, and keep both labels explicit.
unknowns: No touch-usability study was performed, so the impact is based on measured hit areas and visible affordance.
The saved evidence does not establish which of the two homepage actions is intended to be primary.
specialist_interpretation: The contrast with the two product pages is useful positive evidence: ADDP already uses large mobile purchase controls in the same site experience, so the homepage inconsistency is visible to both self-purchasers and adult-child researchers.
limitations: The comparison uses stabilized screenshots and computed rectangles at one mobile viewport per page.
The homepage had a material initial-to-stabilized visual difference, so only the stabilized state supports this finding.
No click outcome is claimed; persona journey navigation errors were excluded as possible audit-induced behavior.

title: The two homepage hero CTAs share a non-directional hash target

title: Purchase CTAs appear before any visible price on both principal product pages
observation: On the stabilized Glucare Plus page, the purchase CTA is visible in the first viewport while the first price-bearing product sample appears farther down the captured page. The captured mobile CTA begins around y=484 px, while the first price-bearing product sample appears around y=1,744 px; the desktop capture shows the same sequence, with the price-bearing sample below the first viewport.

impact.user: A high-intent self-purchaser or adult child cannot evaluate the advertised offer price before choosing the prominent purchase action.
impact.business: Price uncertainty is introduced at the strongest buying prompt on two critical product routes, increasing the amount of exploration needed before a purchase decision.

suggested_direction: Place the current price, package or quantity, and any promotion terms beside each primary hero CTA. If the CTA jumps to multiple offer cards, state that clearly and summarize the starting price or available package range before the action.
unknowns: The captured heroes do not identify which downstream package each primary CTA is intended to represent.
The evidence does not establish promotion duration or eligibility.
specialist_interpretation: The product identity and primary action are strong, especially on mobile, but both purchase audiences must act or scroll without first seeing the commercial terms. This is a price-visibility issue; it does not question the products' health claims or suitability.
limitations: Price-bearing product cards are present farther down both pages and are preserved as positive evidence.
The finding is based on stabilized screenshots and captured element coordinates, not on an order attempt.
No cart, checkout, payment, account, or form mutation was performed.

title: Product landing pages fragment the ADDP visual identity
observation: The captured Glucare Plus product page uses a cream, brown and gold palette across its main sections, while the captured ADDP homepage uses navy, white and warm yellow accents. The shared logo and global header remain visible on both pages, but the main Glucare product sections do not repeat the homepage palette prominently.

impact.user: Moving from the homepage into different products can feel like entering separate campaign sites, increasing the effort required to recognize that the same company stands behind each offer.
impact.business: The visual split weakens portfolio coherence and reduces the transfer of trust built on the ADDP homepage to individual product propositions.

suggested_direction: Define a shared ADDP product-page frame using recurring navy brand anchors, typography, trust modules, and portfolio cues, while retaining controlled product-specific accent colors for Glucare Plus and Dovital.
unknowns: No separate brand-standards document or source logo palette was included in the allowed inputs; consistency was assessed from the checklist and rendered pages.
The Viên An Đường product page was not present in the collected inventory, so the three-product system could not be compared in full.
specialist_interpretation: For both a self-purchaser and an adult child comparing products for a parent, consistent ADDP ownership matters because trust must carry from company to product. The current pages show product personality clearly, but ADDP's portfolio identity becomes much less dominant inside the two captured product experiences.
limitations: This is a visual-consistency assessment of stabilized captures. It does not assert a source-level cause, and the partial render status means unseen or unresolved assets may affect some lower-page details.

title: Visible safety and standards claims lack identifiable proof
observation: The homepage trust strip states "Chứng nhận an toàn" and "Sản phẩm đạt tiêu chuẩn chất lượng và an toàn" beside a generic badge icon, but the stabilized homepage evidence does not show a named certificate, standard identifier, issuer, or public document. The separate company page introduces a "Tiêu chuẩn" section while its four intended standard visuals render as pale generic placeholder tiles; the rendered HTML lists those images with empty alternative text.

impact.user: A skeptical buyer researching for a parent can see that safety and standards are asserted but cannot identify what credential or standard the visible claim refers to, limiting informed trust.
impact.business: Generic claims and placeholder-like standards imagery reduce the credibility value that visible certification or quality evidence could provide at a key decision point.

suggested_direction: Replace generic proof cues with readable, named credential or standard details, contextual captions, and public supporting documents where the company can substantiate them; ensure the company-page visuals render as identifiable evidence rather than placeholders.
unknowns: The run does not establish whether supporting certificates or documents exist elsewhere outside the collected paths.
Whether the pale tiles are source images or render-time fallbacks is unknown; no implementation cause is asserted.
The authenticity or validity of any certificate, standard, or health claim was not assessed.
specialist_interpretation: For an older or middle-aged buyer, the short trust strip is easy to scan, but it remains an assertion. For an adult child doing deeper diligence, the company page is the natural place to verify the claim, and the visible standards area does not provide identifiable evidence in this run.
limitations: This finding is limited to what is visibly named or rendered in the saved homepage and company-page evidence. It does not infer certification authenticity, health validity, backend state, or the absence of documents beyond the collected scope.
